title: Medication Administration Protocol
content: Section 1: Scope - Standard inpatient medication administration for registered nurses. Section 2: Procedure - Verify patient ID band using 3 points of identification. Section 3: High-Alert Medications - Double check insulin and heparin with a second nurse. Section 4: Documentation - Log immediately in paper chart or legacy EHR.

title: Medication Administration Protocol
content: Section 1: Scope - Standard inpatient medication administration. Section 2: Procedure - Mandatory barcode medication scanning prior to administration. Section 3: High-Alert Medications - Independent dual-nurse signoff for IV push anticoagulants, narcotics, and insulin infusions. Section 4: Pediatric Titration - Weight-based calculation using milligrams per kilogram rounded to two decimal places.

title: Medication Administration Protocol
content: Section 1: Scope - Hospital-wide medication safety guidelines for inpatient wards and ICUs. Section 2: Procedure - Scan patient barcode and medication packaging with smart-pump wireless verification. Section 3: High-Alert Medications - Independent two-practitioner dual signoff mandatory for IV push potassium, concentrated electrolytes, and opioids. Section 4: Pediatric Titration - Weight-based calculation with maximum single-dose capping per pharmacy formulary.

title: Medication Administration Protocol
content: Section 1: Scope - Current clinical standard for all inpatient wards, emergency units, and critical care areas. Section 2: Five Rights Verification - Confirm right patient, right medication, right dose, right route, right time. Section 3: High-Alert Medications - Dual independent electronic verification mandatory for intravenous insulin, unfractionated heparin, and IV push concentrated opioids. Section 4: Pediatric Titration & Dose Limits - Strict mg/kg weight-based calculations with automated EHR hard-stop dose limits and mandatory pharmacist verification. Section 5: Emergency Exception - Verbal orders permitted only during active resuscitation under attending physician command.

title: Infection Prevention & PPE Protocol
content: Section 1: Standard Precautions - Hand hygiene before and after patient contact. Section 2: PPE - Disposable surgical masks in respiratory triage areas.

title: Infection Prevention & PPE Protocol
content: Section 1: Standard Precautions - Alcohol-based rub 30 seconds minimum. Section 2: Contact Precautions - Gown and gloves for MRSA/VRE. Section 3: Airborne Precautions - N95 respirator and negative pressure room for pulmonary tuberculosis.

title: Infection Prevention & PPE Protocol
content: Section 1: Universal Infection Control - Hand hygiene using hospital-approved chlorhexidine or 70% alcohol rubs prior to entering patient zones. Section 2: Enhanced Contact Isolation - Single-use gowns and nitrile gloves for enteric pathogens (C. difficile requires soap and water handwashing, not alcohol). Section 3: Airborne & Aerosol Precautions - Fitted N95 or PAPR respirator in verified negative-pressure airborne infection isolation rooms (AIIR). Section 4: Donning and Doffing Sequence - Dedicated ante-room doffing with hand hygiene between glove and gown removal. Section 5: Decontamination - Quaternary ammonium disinfectant wipes with 3-minute wet contact time for IT workstations, computer keyboards, and patient ward equipment.

title: Adult Resuscitation & Code Blue Protocol
content: Section 1: Basic Life Support - Chest compressions 100-120 bpm at depth of 2 inches. Section 2: Defibrillation - Monophasic shock at 360 Joules. Section 3: Medications - Epinephrine 1mg IV every 3-5 minutes.

title: Adult Resuscitation & Code Blue Protocol
content: Section 1: Code Blue Activation - Immediate overhead paging and high-performance CPR team dispatch. Section 2: High-Quality Compressions - Rate 100-120 per minute, depth 5-6 cm with full recoil and CPR metronome feedback; rotate compressor every 2 minutes. Section 3: Biphasic Defibrillation - 200 Joules synchronized biphasic shock for VF/pVT; resume CPR immediately. Section 4: Pharmacotherapy - Epinephrine 1 mg IV/IO every 3-5 minutes; Amiodarone 300 mg bolus for refractory VF/pVT followed by 150 mg second dose. Section 5: Post-Arrest Targeted Temperature Management - Maintain 32-36 degrees Celsius for comatose survivors.

title: Adult Resuscitation & Code Blue Protocol

title: Pediatric Sepsis Triage Protocol
content: Section 1: Screening - Assess fever > 38.5C and tachycardia. Section 2: Fluid Resuscitation - Normal saline bolus 20 ml/kg over 1 hour.

title: Pediatric Sepsis Triage Protocol
content: Section 1: Rapid Clinical Triage - Screen high-risk pediatric triggers: abnormal heart rate, delayed capillary refill > 3s, altered mental state, or purpuric rash. Section 2: Sepsis Golden Hour Bundle - Obtain blood cultures prior to broad-spectrum IV antibiotics; complete antibiotic administration within 60 minutes. Section 3: Volume Resuscitation - Balanced crystalloid bolus 10-20 mL/kg infused over 10 to 20 minutes, reassessing closely for hepatomegaly and crackles. Section 4: Vasoactive Support - Initiate early epinephrine infusion (0.05-0.3 mcg/kg/min) for fluid-refractory cold shock; norepinephrine for warm shock. Section 5: Escalation - Immediate pediatric ICU consultation upon second bolus requirement.

title: Surgical Safety & Timeout Procedure
content: Section 1: Pre-Op Verification - Check consent form. Section 2: Timeout - Verbal pause prior to incision.

title: Surgical Safety & Timeout Procedure
content: Section 1: Sign In (Before induction) - Patient confirms identity, site marking, and procedure; anesthesia safety check completed; pulse oximeter functioning. Section 2: Time Out (Immediately before incision) - Entire surgical team halts activity; verbal confirmation of all team members, patient name, procedure, exact anatomical site, antibiotic prophylaxis within 60 mins, essential imaging displayed. Section 3: Sign Out (Before leaving OR) - Instrument, sponge, and needle counts verified; specimen labeled with two patient identifiers; post-op recovery plan reviewed.

title: Controlled Substance Waste & Destruction
content: Section 1: Chain of Custody - All Schedule II and III controlled substances dispensed must be tracked via automated dispensing cabinets (ADC). Section 2: Dual Witness Disposal - Any unused narcotic portion must be immediately rendered unrecoverable using chemical denaturing solution in the presence of two licensed nurses or one pharmacist and one nurse. Section 3: Discrepancy Reporting - Unresolved counts exceeding 0.1 mL or 1 tablet must be escalated to Pharmacy Director and Hospital Security within 2 hours.

title: ICU Mechanical Ventilation Weaning
content: Section 1: Daily Spontaneous Breathing Trial (SBT) - Assess readiness criteria: PaO2/FiO2 > 150, PEEP <= 8 cmH2O, hemodynamically stable without active ischemia. Section 2: SBT Execution - 30 to 120 minutes on pressure support <= 7 cmH2O or T-piece. Section 3: Failure Triggers - Respiratory rate > 35 bpm, SpO2 < 90%, heart rate change > 20%, diaphoresis or agitation. Section 4: Extubation Readiness - Adequate cough reflex, minimal endotracheal secretions, and negative cuff leak test if risk of laryngeal edema.

title: Hospital Visitor and Caregiver Policy
content: Section 1: Visiting Hours - General inpatient wards open 08:00 to 20:00 daily. Section 2: Designated Caregivers - Up to two designated family caregivers permitted 24/7 bedside access in pediatric and ICU units. Section 3: Infection Precautions - Visitors must perform hand hygiene and wear surgical masks if symptomatic.
